newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile government in crisis over prison break-out.
newsitem.headline: Chile government in crisis over prison break-out.

text.p: The Chilean government faced a deepening political crisis on Tuesday as police mounted a massive manhunt for four leftist guerrillas who made a dramatic escape by helicopter from a top-security jail.

Prison director Claudio Martinez resigned in disgrace on Tuesday over the break-out and the Interior and Justice Ministers said their offers of resignation had been turned down by President Eduardo Frei.

The escape came just weeks after controversy over alleged links between the government and terrorist groups following charges that a police chief and minister obstructed a probe into leftist guerrilla activity in the early 1990s.
"The government and all of us look ridiculous," said Senator Sergio Bitar of the centre-left Partido por La Democracia.
"We have all been stupid to have believed that terrorism has been eradicated."

The turmoil triggered by the break-out caused Frei to delay his televised end-of-year message to the nation that was to have been broadcast on Monday. He was to broadcast his message on Tuesday evening.
Police were combing the southern suburbs of Santiago and the nearby foothills of the Andes for the prisoners, who are all members of the leftist group Manuel Rodriguez Patriotic Front.

The convicts have been identified as Ricardo Palma, Mauricio Hernandez, Pablo Munoz and Patricio Ortiz. Palma and Hernandez, both leaders of the front, were serving life sentences for crimes including the assassination of rightist senator Jaime Guzman in 1991 and the kidnapping of a newspaper magnate's son, Cristian Edwards.
The Front, one of several guerrilla groups active in Chile in recent years, was responsible for the failed assassination attempt against former military ruler Augusto Pinochet in 1986.
Right-wing politicians reacted with outrage to news of the convicts' escape and attacked the government's handling of the situation.
"I think this is a national disgrace. It is now time for the government to assume its responsibility," said rightist politician Juan Antonio Coloma.
"The escape is frankly extraordinary and disillusioning."

The four men made their daring getaway by scrambling into a basket lowered onto the prison by the helicopter in the middle of a gunfire battle between the aircraft's occupants and prison guards on the ground.
The helicopter had been fitted with anti-bullet plating on one side to protect it from shots from the guards.

The helicopter had been hired from an airfield in Santiago by five people, including three women who appeared to be from the United States and two men with strong Argentine accents, according to officials from the hire company.

The helicopter flew to a spot just south of Santiago, where the pilot, a serving police officer, was tied up and left in a house and someone else took over the helm. The pilot later escaped and raised the alarm.
Police said they found the helicopter and a getaway car with two M-16 rifles in a park in the south of the city.
The second getaway vehicle used by the group has not been found, they said.
